key_insight: This randomized trial protocol will compare Nabla with Epic’s ambient AI documentation solution; no comparative results are reported yet.
clinical_relevance: The study could inform health-system decisions about ambient AI usability, documentation workflows, and clinician experience.
method: Randomize 374 UCLA Health ambulatory clinicians with active Nabla licenses 1:1 to two parallel arms.
Run November 9, 2026–January 17, 2027, including a four-week lead-in.
Compare follow-up System Usability Scale scores using intention-to-treat mixed-effects models.
evidence_signal: The planned primary endpoint is clinician-rated usability, with additional evaluation of documentation burden, EHR time, adoption, coding patterns, and patient-reported communication.
watch_item: A single-system sample of clinicians already licensed for Nabla may limit generalizability to other settings or first-time users.
paper_title: Randomized Trial Protocol: Head-to-Head Comparison of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Documentation Tools on Clinician Usability
